key_idea: Each adjacent pair of words gives one edge (first differing letters); the alphabet is unique iff the topological order is forced at every step.
sketch: Compare only adjacent words: at the first differing position add edge a->b; if the later word is a proper prefix of the earlier one the list is IMPOSSIBLE. Run Kahn's algorithm over all letters a..L (including letters that never appear). If not all letters are output there is a cycle -> IMPOSSIBLE; otherwise if the queue ever held more than one candidate -> AMBIGUOUS; else print the order. O(N*len + 26^2). Pitfalls: IMPOSSIBLE takes priority over AMBIGUOUS, deduplicate edges before counting indegrees, and unused letters make the answer ambiguous.
